sights.name: Tivoli Gardens
sights.fact: Opened in 1843, Tivoli is often called the world's second-oldest amusement park still running. The oldest, Bakken from 1583, lies about 10 km to the north.
sights.imageAlt: Line drawing of a domed gate arch between two brick pavilions, with a roller coaster and a pagoda tower behind.
sights.author: Claude (AI), after a photo by Sissew
sights.licence: CC0 1.0 (AI-generated; any rights waived by the Worldbound team)

sights.name: Nyhavn canal tour
sights.fact: Nyhavn was dug in the 1670s as a canal linking the harbour to the city centre. Hans Christian Andersen lived in three of its houses.
sights.imageAlt: Line drawing of a row of wide, colourful canal houses seen straight on, with parasols on the quay and moored ships.
sights.author: Claude (AI), after a photo by Jorge Láscar

sights.name: Eiffel Tower
sights.fact: The Eiffel Tower was built for the 1889 World's Fair. It was the tallest structure in the world until 1930.
sights.imageAlt: Line drawing of a wrought-iron lattice tower with a great arch between its legs, above trees and long lawns.
sights.author: Claude (AI), after a public-domain photo
sights.licence: CC0 1.0 (AI-generated; any rights waived by the Worldbound team)

sights.name: Louvre
sights.fact: The Louvre was a royal palace before it opened as a public museum in 1793. Its glass pyramid entrance was completed in 1989.
sights.imageAlt: Line drawing of a glass pyramid in a paved court, framed by palace wings with domed corner pavilions.
sights.author: Claude (AI), after a photo by Benh LIEU SONG

sights.name: Tower of London
sights.fact: The Tower of London was founded after the Norman Conquest of 1066. Today it holds the Crown Jewels of the United Kingdom.
sights.imageAlt: Line drawing of a square stone keep with four lead-domed turrets, behind a battlemented wall on the river.
sights.author: Claude (AI), after a photo by Bob Collowan

sights.name: British Museum
sights.fact: Founded in 1753, the British Museum opened to the public in 1759. It is home to the Rosetta Stone.
sights.imageAlt: Line drawing of a museum front: a columned portico with a sculpted pediment between two colonnaded wings.
sights.author: Claude (AI), after a photo by Yair Haklai

sights.name: Colosseum
sights.fact: The Colosseum was completed in AD 80 under Emperor Titus. It could hold an estimated 50,000 spectators.
sights.imageAlt: Line drawing of a ruined amphitheatre: a tall outer wall with a sloping buttress beside lower tiers of arches.
sights.author: Claude (AI), after a photo by Nicholas Hartmann

sights.name: Vatican Museums
sights.fact: The Vatican Museums trace their origins to Pope Julius II in the early 1500s. Their route includes the Sistine Chapel, whose ceiling Michelangelo painted from 1508 to 1512.
sights.imageAlt: Line drawing of a double spiral staircase seen from the top, its ornate railings winding down to a small floor.
sights.author: Claude (AI), after a photo by gnuckx
sights.licence: CC0 1.0 (AI-generated; any rights waived by the Worldbound team)

sights.name: Topkapı Palace
sights.fact: Topkapı Palace was the main residence of the Ottoman sultans for nearly 400 years. It became a museum in 1924.
sights.imageAlt: Line drawing of a palace gate with a rounded arch between two octagonal towers with tall pointed caps.
sights.author: Claude (AI), after a photo by Maksym Kozlenko

sights.name: Galata Tower
sights.fact: The Galata Tower was built in 1348 as part of the walls of the Genoese colony of Galata.
sights.imageAlt: Line drawing of a round stone tower with an arched gallery, a balcony and a tall conical cap, above apartment blocks.
sights.author: Claude (AI), after a photo by A.Savin

sights.name: Statue of Liberty
sights.fact: The Statue of Liberty was a gift from France and was dedicated in 1886. Its copper skin turned green over time as a patina formed.
sights.imageAlt: Line drawing of a robed statue raising a torch on a tall granite pedestal, above star-shaped fort walls.
sights.author: Claude (AI), after a photo by Dietmar Rabich

sights.name: Empire State Building
sights.fact: The Empire State Building opened in 1931 after just over 13 months of construction. It was the tallest building in the world until 1970.
sights.imageAlt: Line drawing of an Art Deco skyscraper seen from the street, its setbacks stepping up to a slim mast.
sights.author: Claude (AI), after a photo by BigMac

sights.name: Senso-ji
sights.fact: Senso-ji is Tokyo's oldest temple, traditionally dated to 628. Visitors enter through the Kaminarimon, or Thunder Gate.
sights.imageAlt: Line drawing of a temple gate with one large curved tiled roof, four columns and a huge paper lantern.
sights.author: Claude (AI), after a public-domain photo
sights.licence: CC0 1.0 (AI-generated; any rights waived by the Worldbound team)

sights.name: Tokyo Skytree
sights.fact: Tokyo Skytree is 634 metres tall and opened in 2012. It is the tallest tower in Japan.
sights.imageAlt: Line drawing of a tall lattice tower with two observation decks, behind riverside towers and an elevated road.
sights.author: Claude (AI), after a photo by Basile Morin

sights.name: Sydney Opera House
sights.fact: The Sydney Opera House, designed by Danish architect Jørn Utzon, opened in 1973. It became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2007.
sights.imageAlt: Line drawing of tall, sail-like tiled shells on a granite podium, seen from a curved promenade by the water.
sights.author: Claude (AI), after a photo by Kgbo

sights.name: Harbour Bridge
sights.fact: The Sydney Harbour Bridge opened in 1932. Its steel arch spans 503 metres, and it is nicknamed 'the Coathanger'.
sights.imageAlt: Line drawing of a steel arch bridge seen at an angle, rising from tall granite pylons over a harbour.
sights.author: Claude (AI), after a photo by Diliff
